subject: Materials Science
title: The Interface: Where Composites Win or Lose
description: A quick win: understand The Interface: Where Composites Win or Lose.

hook.text: The strongest fiber in the weakest bond is just expensive filler.

buildup.text: The interface is where fiber meets matrix — stress must transfer smoothly across it.

discovery.text: Sizing agents coat fibers before embedding — they're chemical matchmakers for fiber and matrix.

twist.text: Too strong an interface makes the composite brittle — cracks blast straight through both materials.

climax.text: A tuned interface lets fibers pull out gradually, absorbing energy and toughening the composite.

punchline.text: The invisible boundary between fiber and matrix decides everything.

quiz.question: Why is a moderate interface strength preferable in composites?
options: It allows fiber pullout that absorbs energy and adds toughness
It reduces the weight of the composite
